engine: PostgreSQL 18.6 (PGlite 0.5.11) on wasm32-unknown-emscripten, compiled by emcc (Emscripten gcc/clang-like replacement + linker emulating GNU ld) 3.1.74 (1092ec30a3fb1d46b1782ff1b4db5094d3d06ae5), 32-bit

checks.name: A deliberately destructive synthetic migration is rejected and all data/schema changes roll back
Security migration preserves every existing public-table row unchanged as normalized JSON
Account 0 sees only its own complete snapshot
Account 0 cannot read another account schedule/medications/doses/budget/location
Account 0 cannot modify/delete/reassign another account
Account 0 cannot read another account schedule/medications/doses/budget/location
Account 0 cannot modify/delete/reassign another account
Account 0 cannot access unused legacy tables or privileged RPCs
Account 1 sees only its own complete snapshot
Account 1 cannot read another account schedule/medications/doses/budget/location
Account 1 cannot modify/delete/reassign another account
Account 1 cannot read another account schedule/medications/doses/budget/location
Account 1 cannot modify/delete/reassign another account
Account 1 cannot access unused legacy tables or privileged RPCs
Account 2 sees only its own complete snapshot
Account 2 cannot read another account schedule/medications/doses/budget/location
Account 2 cannot modify/delete/reassign another account
Account 2 cannot read another account schedule/medications/doses/budget/location
Account 2 cannot modify/delete/reassign another account
Account 2 cannot access unused legacy tables or privileged RPCs
Anonymous identity cannot read/write snapshots, credentials, audit or privileged RPCs
Missing authoritative identity cannot read or save records
Account switching cannot send an old owner save under the new identity
Forged ownership fields and role metadata do not grant another account access
Concurrent stale revisions cannot overwrite a newer snapshot
Earlier synthetic backup restores as a new revision and leaves history intact
Device registration is atomic, requires prior keys before account switching, and is owner-scoped on disable
Independent device rate limit accepts only its budget
Existing synthetic B/C records survive the security migration and attempted attacks unchanged
A full disposable database archive restores snapshots, history, audit, grants and RLS to a second database

limitations: Auth/GoTrue JWT signature, expiry and refresh are not simulated by database role tests.
Cron and Vault schemas are isolated stubs; no external calls or production records are used.
PGlite has one connection; real multi-connection transaction contention needs staging Supabase validation.
